videos.title: The Curve Left by a Quiet Thread #math #Shorts

editorial.opening: A taut thread begins drawing immediately; the object gives the curve a visible cause.
editorial.mechanism: Tangent and arc length are shown separately; one-to-two released units distinguish thread length from distance to the center.
editorial.readability: Larger spool and muted earlier trace keep the active arc visible; captions sit below the construction.
editorial.pacing: Measured pauses at tangency and length comparison; the explicitly narrated rewind permits a new measurement.
editorial.sound: Dry local narration. All full ASR transcripts reviewed. Homophone, article, number-formatting and curve-name transcription differences were read against the intended script; no mathematical change identified. No subjective listening.
editorial.remaining_weaknesses: The final curve is attractive as geometry but the film still has a sparse diagrammatic setting. An isolated still does not communicate the mechanism.

videos.title: Two Straight Tracks and One Gentle Curve #math #Shorts

editorial.opening: Two constrained sliders create a curved trace from straight tracks.
editorial.mechanism: The pen divides the fixed bar one-to-two, producing unequal horizontal/vertical reach; moving it to the midpoint gives a circle.
editorial.readability: The earlier ellipse remains subdued behind the circle; one active color carries the new trace.
editorial.pacing: The drawing pauses to compare the two reaches before completing the contour.

editorial.remaining_weaknesses: Viewers must follow several moving points. The tiny slider bodies and purely technical setting may limit emotional appeal.

videos.title: The Rods That Quietly Copy a Shape #math #Shorts

editorial.opening: Two points leave matching shapes at different scales.
editorial.mechanism: Similar triangles explain the enlargement; a small triangle visibly scales about the fixed pivot before the linkage resumes.
editorial.readability: Plain-language side relation replaces small A/D labels and symbolic ratios. Fixed pivot and copying points remain distinct.
editorial.pacing: Motion alternates with a longer explanatory pause; a reverse tracing role ends with a half-size copy.
editorial.sound: Dry local narration. All full ASR transcripts reviewed. Homophone, article, number-formatting and curve-name transcription differences were read against the intended script; no mathematical change identified. No subjective listening.
editorial.remaining_weaknesses: The linkage is the most cognitively demanding construction here. Parallel directions and similar triangles may still need slower explanation for a novice.

videos.title: The Curve at the End of a Taut Thread #math #Shorts

editorial.opening: A taut thread pulls a point behind a straight moving end.
editorial.mechanism: The thread gives the tangent direction and fixed tangent length; a shorter thread leaves a comparison trace closer to the guide.
editorial.readability: The guide was centered; original and shorter traces remain distinguishable.
editorial.pacing: The tangent is inspected at rest, then motion resumes; the restart is explicitly narrated.

videos.title: The Same Step Can Reach Different Heights #math #Shorts

editorial.opening: A fixed step rotates with a ray and leaves an unexpected curve.
editorial.mechanism: Upright versus sixty-degree steps compare full and half projected height; a perpendicular-step comparison reveals a different locus.
editorial.readability: The larger step makes the height comparison visible; neutral labels during rotation prevent a premature half-height claim.
editorial.pacing: The important tilt is completed before the half-height statement; two direction rules are compared before returning to the original trace.
editorial.sound: Dry local narration. All full ASR transcripts reviewed. Homophone, article, number-formatting and curve-name transcription differences were read against the intended script; no mathematical change identified. No subjective listening.
editorial.remaining_weaknesses: The unfamiliar name conchoid is optional vocabulary; viewers may retain only the more useful distinction between length and vertical height.
